components.name: Strip
components.description: A game as one trace on a literal scale: one small box is 5% chances, height is 20 boxes.
components.css: .ds-strip { position:relative;width:480px;height:160px;background-color:var(--salmon);background-image:linear-gradient(rgb(var(--grid) / 0.42) 1px,transparent 1px),linear-gradient(90deg,rgb(var(--grid) / 0.42) 1px,transparent 1px),linear-gradient(rgb(var(--grid) / 0.2) 1px,transparent 1px),linear-gradient(90deg,rgb(var(--grid) / 0.2) 1px,transparent 1px);background-size:40px 40px,40px 40px,8px 8px,8px 8px;box-shadow:inset 0 1px 0 var(--ink),inset 0 -1px 0 var(--ink); } .ds-strip svg { position:absolute;inset:0;width:100%;height:100%;overflow:visible; } .ds-strip-mid { position:absolute;inset:50% 0 auto;height:1px;background:var(--ink);opacity:0.55; } .ds-strip-here { position:absolute;top:0;bottom:0;left:calc(64% - 8px);width:16px;background:var(--marker); } .ds-strip-head { position:absolute;top:0;bottom:0;left:64%;width:1.5px;background:var(--ink); } .ds-strip-trace, .ds-strip-fall { fill:none;vector-effect:non-scaling-stroke;stroke-linecap:round;stroke-linejoin:round; } .ds-strip-trace { stroke:var(--ink);stroke-width:1.75px; } .ds-strip-fall { stroke:var(--red);stroke-width:3px; }

narrative.overview:
Coachmate draws every chess game as a strip of chart paper. The player's chances print from left to right as one ink line, and the reader's job is to find where that line fell. The strip is how you move through a game. The board follows it.

The material is a roll of saturated salmon paper under a kitchen light, marked up with a pen. The surface is printed and flat, with one continuous thread of data and short notes written in its margin. Density comes from showing every game at once as a labelled row. Ruled lines divide the page, so nothing needs a box around it.

Colour is committed. Salmon carries the landing page, and every working screen sits on a paler pink so the task leads. The system is light only, because the scene it comes from is lit paper. It must never read as a SaaS dashboard or as a copy of Chess.com's Game Review.
keyCharacteristics: A game always appears as a strip, with a literal vertical scale.
Three inks with fixed jobs, plus signal red for the fall.
Heavy condensed Archivo headings over tabular Archivo text.
Hairline ink rules with sharp corners and no raised surfaces.
Motion that feeds paper and draws pen lines.

rules.name: The Three Inks Rule
rules.body: Thermal black is the engine, ballpoint blue is the coach and highlighter yellow is "you are here". A new element takes an ink by who is speaking, and a colour is never added for variety. Blue has one mechanical exception: the focus ring, the text caret and the keyboard cursor on the board are the pen in the user's hand.

rules.name: The Fall Rule
rules.body: Signal red appears only on blunders and the falling trace. Errors, warnings, destructive actions and low clocks do not get red. A low clock inverts to a thermal black block.

rules.name: The No Paler Rule
rules.body: The Operate ground is #fbe9e3 and must go no paler. Below that the page turns to cream and the world is gone. Lifted Paper is a fill for small parts inside a screen and never a page ground.

rules.name: The Print Figure Rule
rules.body: All text sets tabular figures from the body down, so numbers hold their columns and change in place.

rules.name: The Margin Note Rule
rules.body: The hand is for a few words written in the margin, such as "it turned here" or "nice". It is always blue and never carries instructions or sentences.

rules.name: The Box Rule
rules.body: Every layout measure is a multiple of 8px. Inline half steps, text leading and pen marks sit outside it.

rules.name: The Literal Scale Rule
rules.body: One small box on a strip equals 5% chances, and a strip plot is always 20 × `--s-box` tall. The bold line sits at 50%, and a heavier grid line falls every five boxes. Change the size only by changing `--s-box` and `--s-height` together. The shipped pairs are 8px and 160px, 6px and 120px, 5.6px and 112px, and 2.4px and 48px.

rules.name: The Flat Paper Rule
rules.body: Blur is never used for depth. If an element needs separating, give it a hairline ink rule or a change of paper.

rules.name: The No Future Rule
rules.body: The drill strip does not scrub. Scrubbing would show moves played after the position the player is solving. It sits at that position as a fixed mark, with a link out to the game for anyone who wants to see the rest.

rules.name: The Feed And Pen Rule
rules.body: Paper feeds, pens draw and pieces slide. Numbers change in place and never count up, and nothing bounces or fades up on entry.

dos: Do choose an ink by who is speaking: thermal black for the engine, ballpoint blue for the coach, highlighter yellow for "you are here".
Do draw every game with the shared strip and keep one small box equal to 5% chances, with the plot 20 × `--s-box` tall.
Do keep every Operate surface on #fbe9e3 or deeper.
Do separate content with 1px ink rules and Hairline dividers, with layout measures in multiples of 8px.
Do show highlighter yellow behind the words or square it marks, as a flat swipe.
Do pair every quality colour with its glyph, since move quality is never carried by colour alone.
Do make state changes discrete, with numbers changing in place.
Do give every new animation a `prefers-reduced-motion` state that shows the finished result.
Do label sample data as bot games wherever it appears.
Do keep Stockfish's GPLv3 licence and credit with `public/engine/`.
donts: Don't use cards, pills, tiles or soft shadows.
Don't add a dark theme. Black printed blocks and the closing landing band are part of the light paper world.
Don't use signal red for errors, warnings, destructive actions or decoration. It belongs to blunders and the falling trace.
Don't use yellow for hover or emphasis, or blue for general links and accents.
Don't let a drill strip scrub, because it would show moves played after the position being solved.
Don't go paler than #fbe9e3 for a page ground, and don't let it drift to cream or white.
Don't resize a strip by height alone, since that breaks the literal scale.
Don't animate figures counting up, or add bounce or fade-up entrances.
Don't put the hand in sentences, instructions or any colour but blue.
Don't invent stats, Elo ranges or speed claims to fill a print line.
